'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[June 2021 Mogadishu bombing]]
***A [[suicide bomber]] [[detonate]]s his explosives at a [[Somali Armed Forces|military]] camp in [[Mogadishu]] where new recruits were queueing outside the camp, killing 15 people and injuring many others. This is the deadliest attack in Mogadishu since [[December 2019 Mogadishu bombing|December 2019]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/15/somalia (Al Jazeera English)]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**The anti-[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|coup]] [[militia]] group Karenni National Defence Force announces that it has stopped its operations against the [[Tatmadaw|Burmese military]] following pleas by civilians residing in the areas they operate in, which have seen 100,000 civilians [[forced displacement|displaced]]. The group says that it will continue its opposition to the [[State Administration Council|military junta]] through other means. Additionally, deposed leader [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] appears in court for the second day, and was reported to be in "better condition". [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/myanmar-militia-group-halts-attacks-troops-after-peace-plea-2021-06-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**36 people are injured in a [[car bomb]] attack on a [[U.S. military]] [[military base|base]] in [[Colombia]]. The [[Colombian government]] suspects possible self-attribution for the attack to the [[National Liberation Army (Colombia)|National Liberation Army]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/car-bomb-explosion-colombia-military-base-injures-23-military-sources-2021-06-15/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Australia–United Kingdom Free Trade Agreement]]
**The [[British government]] announces that a [[free trade agreement]] has been reached between [[Australia]] and the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-57478412 (BBC News)]
*[[Censorship in India]], [[Violence against Muslims in India]]
**The [[Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology|Indian Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology]] strips [[Twitter]] of legal protection from prosecution after the social media site refuses to take down a tweet featuring a video of an elderly [[Islam in India|Muslim]] man in [[Ghaziabad]] being assaulted by a [[Hindu]] mob and being forced to chant "[[Jai Shri Ram]]". [[Uttar Pradesh]] police, who demanded the removal of the tweet, alleges the video was "misleading". [https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/twitter-loses-legal-indemnity-for-not-complying-with-new-it-rules-can-be-charged-for-users-posts-say-government-sources-2464846 (NDTV)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Israel]] lifts its indoor [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|face mask requirement]] for those except unvaccinated people in healthcare facilities, airplane passengers, and people who must [[quarantine]] as the number of new cases continues to decline. [https://www.ynetnews.com/article/SkijzjHi00 (Ynetnews)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/israel-to-drop-indoor-mask-requirement-from-tuesday-as-daily-cases-near-zero/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Malaysia]]
****The [[Malaysia]]n Drug Control Authority grants a conditional approval for emergency use of the [[CanSino]] [[Convidecia]] and [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine|Johnson & Johnson]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]s. The [[Government of Malaysia|authorities]] also approve the use of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] vaccine for people over the age of 12. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2021/06/15/govt-approves-pfizer-jabs-for-12-year-olds-and-above-conditional-approval-for-cansino-and-johnson--johnson-vaccines-says-health-dg (''The Star'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oman]]
****The [[Oman]]i Health Ministry reports that the [[Mucormycosis#COVID-19–associated mucormycosis|black fungus infection]] was detected in three patients. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/15/black-fungus-detected-covid-19-patients-oman (Al Jazeera English)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] surpasses 200,000 cases of [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2132623/total-covid-caseload-passes-200-000-tuesday (''Bangkok Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in France]]
****[[France]] begins to [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccinate]] children between the ages of 12 and 18 years old using special child-sized needles in order to achieve [[herd immunity]] and reduce the spread of [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|variant]]s of COVID-19. The age eligibility of 12 years is one of the lowest of any [[European Union]] nation. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/france-vocid-vaccination-children-b1866334.html (''The Independent'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia]]
****[[Slovenia]] declares the end of its eight-month [[state of emergency]], which means that cultural and sports events will be able to reopen at 75% capacity for people who can demonstrate that they have either been vaccinated, [[COVID-19 testing|tested]] negative or have recovered from COVID-19. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-06-15/slovenia-declares-end-of-covid-19-state-of-emergency?context=amp (U.S. News & World Report)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] administers a single-day record of 1.4 million doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]s. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/turkey-administers-record-number-of-covid-vaccine-doses-in-one-day/2275300 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ecuador]]
***[[Ecuador]]'s health regulatory authority Arcsa approves the usage of the [[CanSino]] [[Convidecia]] vaccine. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/ecuador-authorizes-use-chinas-cansino-vaccine-against-covid-19-2021-06-15/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The [[United States]] surpasses 600,000 deaths from COVID-19, even as daily deaths are reported to be decreasing. [https://www.voanews.com/covid-19-pandemic/us-surpasses-600000-deaths-covid-leading-world (Voice of America)] [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-600k-deaths-us-1ef14a0b998e6ce99281edf6e996dfbe (Associated Press)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Cross-Strait relations]]
**The [[Ministry of National Defense (Republic of China)|Taiwanese Defense Ministry]] reports that 28 [[People's Liberation Army Air Force|Chinese air force planes]], including four [[Xian H-6|H-6 bombers]] capable of carrying [[nuclear weapon]]s, entered [[Air defense identification zone#Taiwan|Taiwan's air defense identification zone]] and flew close to the southern tip of the main island and around the [[Pratas Islands]]. This is China's largest incursion since Taiwan began monitoring such activities last year. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/taiwan-reports-largest-incursion-yet-by-chinese-air-force-2021-06-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Armenia–Turkey relations]], [[Azerbaijan–Turkey relations]]
**[[President of Turkey|Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] announces that [[Turkey]] will open a consulate in [[Shusha]], a [[Nagorno-Karabakh]] city captured by [[Azerbaijan]] during [[Second Nagorno-Karabakh War|last year's]] [[war]], and that he will look to co-produce [[Unmanned combat aerial vehicle|military drones]] with Azerbaijan. Both announcements followed his tour of the contested region with [[President of Azerbaijan|Azerbaijani President]] [[Ilham Aliyev]] the same day. The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Armenia)|Armenian Foreign Ministry]] condemns the visit as a provocation. [https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2021/06/erdogan-aliyev-cement-military-and-business-ties-during-karabakh-victory-lap (Al-Monitor)] 

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]], [[2021 Uptown Minneapolis unrest]], [[Killing of Deona Knajdek]]
**Heavily-armed police officers in [[Minneapolis]] begin clearing an [[intersection (road)|intersection]] of Lake Street and Hennepin Avenue in [[Uptown, Minneapolis|Uptown neighborhood]] which had been the site of protests since June 3, when [[Winston Boogie Smith]] was killed by law enforcement. Tensions escalated dramatically since the death of protester Deona Knajdek when she was killed when a speeding car [[Vehicle-ramming attack|rammed into her car]], which she was using to protect protesters. [https://minnesota.cbslocal.com/2021/06/15/minneapolis-police-work-to-reopen-uptown-street-occupied-by-protesters/ (WCCO-TV)]
*[[2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**Seventeen [[Palestinians]] are arrested and 33 more are injured after Israeli police fire tear gas and rubber bullets at Palestinians protesting at the [[Damascus Gate]] over the procession of a march called [[Dance of Flags]] through [[Jerusalem]]'s [[Old City (Jerusalem)|Old City]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/15/tensions-high-in-jerusalem-ahead-of-hardline-israeli-march (Al Jazeera English)]
*[[LGBT rights in Hungary]]
**The [[National Assembly (Hungary)|Hungarian National Assembly]] passes a law banning content depicting or promoting [[same-sex relationship]]s and [[Gender transitioning|gender reassignment]] to anyone under the age of 18. 157 MPs voted in favor, with all opposition parties except the far-right [[Jobbik]] boycotting the vote. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/06/15/mps-in-hungary-back-ban-on-sharing-content-with-children-that-promotes-homosexuality (Euronews)]
*A [[Judiciary of France|French court]] issues the French subsidiary of the Dutch [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]] [[IKEA]] a [[Euro|€]]1 million ([[United States dollar|US$]]1.2 million) fine for conducting illegal [[employee monitoring]] activities on its employees and applicants between 2009 and 2012. Its former [[chief executive officer]] is also given a two-year prison sentence. [https://today.rtl.lu/news/world/a/1738939.html (RTL Télé Lëtzebuerg)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Peruvian general election]]
**[[Pedro Castillo]] of the left-wing [[Free Peru]] party claims victory in the presidential election, with the final tally putting him 44,058 votes ahead of his rival [[Keiko Fujimori]] of the right-wing [[Popular Force]] party. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/perus-castillo-leads-election-with-501-votes-after-all-ballots-tallied-2021-06-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Prime Minister of Australia|Australian Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] denies reports by the [[Australian Broadcasting Company]]'s ''[[Four Corners (Australian TV program)|Four Corners]]'' program that his close friend Tim Stewart, who was referred to the national [[Right-wing terrorism|terror]] hotline by his own family for his extreme [[Far-right politics|far-right]] political views, influenced his decision to mention "[[Satanic ritual abuse|ritual abuse]]" in a speech regarding [[Child sexual abuse in Australia|child sexual abuse]] earlier this year, in line with the [[QAnon|QAnon conspiracy theory]]. [https://www.news.com.au/national/politics/scott-morrison-says-he-wont-answer-the-abcs-questions-on-his-ties-to-qanon/news-story/2d00165b5e9ba5ee83a843bb96c746da (News)]
*[[Vice Chief of the Defence Staff (Canada)|Canadian Vice-Chief of the Defence Staff]] [[Michael Rouleau]] resigns following criticisms of him playing golf with former General [[Jonathan Vance]], who is accused of sexual misconduct. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-57478608 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[UEFA Euro 2020]]
**[[Portugal national football team|Portuguese]] football player [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] becomes the highest-scoring player in the history of the [[UEFA European Championship]], when he scored his 10th and 11th goals in a match against [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]]. He also becomes the first player to score in five different tournaments. [https://www.espn.com/soccer/uefa-european-championship/story/4409326/euro-2020-portugals-cristiano-ronaldo-breaks-goals-record-in-historic-fifth-finals-appearance (ESPN)]
